name: merchant_onboarding
subject: merchant
hold: Should the pending merchant application be held for manual review because it shows signs of a fraudulent merchant, of a stolen business identity, of a merchant that was terminated before, or of a business that hides what it really sells?

typologies.merchant_farm: Merchant farm: one operator opens many merchant accounts from the same network, device or details
typologies.stolen_identity: Stolen business identity: a real business's details are used by someone who does not control it
typologies.reapplication: Returning bad actor: a merchant that was terminated or rejected before applies again under new details
typologies.laundering_front: Transaction laundering: the declared business hides a different, restricted line of business

reasons.linked_to_bad_merchant: The IP address, device, owner or bank account is shared with a merchant that was rejected or terminated
reasons.datacenter_or_vpn_ip: The application comes from a datacenter, VPN or proxy network and not from a business or home connection
reasons.shared_device: The device is shared with other merchant applications
reasons.application_burst: Several merchant applications came from the same IP address or device within a short time
reasons.shared_bank_account: The payout bank account is also used by another merchant
reasons.ip_country_mismatch: The application IP address is in a different country from the business
reasons.email_domain_mismatch: The contact email is on a free or throwaway domain that does not match the business website
reasons.new_or_thin_website: The website was registered very recently or has little real content
reasons.business_mismatch: The website describes a different business from the one declared
reasons.bank_name_mismatch: The bank account holder name does not match the business
reasons.rushed_application: The form was completed unusually fast or with most fields pasted
reasons.document_problem: An identity or business document failed verification
